Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
### Exercise 1: Bank Transfer

Implement thread-safe bank transfers between accounts:

1. Create an Account class with balance and a lock
2. Implement `transfer(from_account, to_account, amount)`
3. Ensure no deadlocks when transferring both ways simultaneously
4. Verify total balance remains constant

### Exercise 2: Read-Write Lock

Implement a read-write lock that:

1. Allows multiple simultaneous readers
2. Allows only one writer (exclusive)
3. Writers have priority over new readers
4. Test with reader and writer threads

### Exercise 3: Producer-Consumer with Condition

Create a multi-producer, multi-consumer system:

1. Bounded buffer of size 5
2. 3 producers, each producing 10 items
3. 2 consumers, consuming until buffer is empty and producers done
4. Use Condition for coordination

### Exercise 4: Barrier Computation

Implement parallel sum:

1. Divide array into N parts (one per thread)
2. Each thread sums its part
3. Use barrier to synchronize
4. After barrier, combine partial sums
5. Compare with sequential sum

### Exercise 5: Timeout Semaphore

Extend Semaphore with timeout:

1. `acquire_with_timeout(seconds)` returns True/False
2. If can't acquire within timeout, return False
3. Test with more acquirers than capacity

### Exercise 6: Event-Based Pipeline

Create a data pipeline with events:

1. Stage 1: Load data (signals when ready)
2. Stage 2: Process data (waits for stage 1, signals when ready)
3. Stage 3: Save results (waits for stage 2)
4. Main thread waits for completion

### Exercise 7: Debounced Timer

Create a debounced function call:

1. If called multiple times rapidly, only last call executes
2. Wait 0.5 seconds after last call before executing
3. Reset timer on each new call
4. Test with 10 rapid calls

### Exercise 8: Lock Hierarchy

Implement a lock hierarchy manager:

1. Each lock has a level (1, 2, 3...)
2. Threads can only acquire higher-level locks while holding lower
3. Raise exception if hierarchy is violated
4. Prevents deadlock by design

### Exercise 9: Semaphore Pool

Create a connection pool using Semaphore:

1. Pool of 5 "connections"
2. `get_connection()` - blocks if none available
3. `release_connection(conn)` - returns to pool
4. Track metrics: wait time, utilization

### Exercise 10: Synchronized Print

Create a thread-safe print function:

1. Uses lock to prevent interleaved output
2. Adds timestamp and thread name
3. Optional: queue-based for non-blocking
4. Test with 10 threads printing simultaneously
